paragraph: Dasaratha in a voice that sounded dispirited and almost extinguishing said "Bogged down in evil if you yet disregard counsel of my minister you will bring upon you, your own destruction. Your deplorable conduct is divorced from all the righteousness. Rule Ayodhya, as you will, along with Bharata. As for me, abandoning my kingdom, my comforts and my wealth, I shall follow Rama."
Situation/Problem_Faced: King Dasaratha, utterly dispirited by Kaikeyi's remorselessness and defiance, foresees her destruction. He relinquishes his kingdom, declaring his intention to abandon all royal comforts and follow Rama into exile, symbolizing his complete despair and rejection of Kaikeyi's actions.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: This passage portrays Dasaratha's profound despair and his ultimate moral stand against Kaikeyi's unrighteousness. It highlights the devastating cost of a broken vow and the king's willingness to sacrifice everything – his kingdom, wealth, and life – to uphold dharma and express solidarity with his beloved son, Rama.
Outcome/Resolution: Dasaratha, having reached the peak of his despair, verbally relinquishes his kingdom and all its comforts, declaring his intention to follow Rama into exile. This represents his ultimate act of protest and self-sacrifice against Kaikeyi's demands and her 'deplorable conduct.' The immediate outcome is Dasaratha's complete moral and emotional withdrawal from his role as king and from his relationship with Kaikeyi, signifying his impending death and the full realization of the curse.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.stress Management: Coping failure, Overwhelmed, Emotional collapse, Self-sacrificial escape, Disintegration
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.anger Management: Resigned despair, Helplessness, Emotional breakdown, Spiritual anguish

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dharma (Righteous Duty - Dasaratha's deep anguish stems from the violation of dharma and his inability to prevent it. His desire to follow Rama signifies his alignment with dharma)
Adharma (Unrighteousness - Kaikeyi's 'deplorable conduct' is explicitly linked to adharma, bringing about her own 'destruction')
Vairagya (Detachment - Dasaratha's decision to abandon kingdom, comforts, and wealth reflects a form of detachment, albeit born of despair rather than spiritual realization)
Tyaga (Sacrifice - Dasaratha's willingness to sacrifice his entire life and royal status out of solidarity with Rama and adherence to righteousness)
Shoka (Grief - His dispirited voice and declaration are direct outcomes of overwhelming shoka)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Dasaratha, engulfed in 'Shoka' (grief) and witnessing the rampant 'Adharma' (unrighteousness) of Kaikeyi, makes a desperate act of 'Tyaga' (sacrifice), abandoning his kingdom and all comforts. His decision to follow Rama into exile, though born of despair, is his ultimate alignment with 'Dharma' and a form of 'Vairagya' (detachment) from worldly life.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, Dasaratha is in a state of profound low mood, sadness, and hopelessness, evident in his 'dispirited' voice and self-destructive intent to abandon everything. His inability to exert control leads to a complete failure of stress management. This also marks the final collapse of his relationship with Kaikeyi, as he effectively divorces himself from her actions and fate. He is experiencing deep grief and loss on multiple levels, choosing a path of self-imposed despair over a kingdom tainted by injustice.
